claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level breaks the document outline: tools that slice the transcription by heading treat 5.11.4 as a sibling of clause 5.11 rather than a subclause of it.
claim.note: The subclause heading 5.11.4 is transcribed at level 2 (##), the level of the clause heading 5.11 THE RENAMES CLAUSE. Its siblings are level 3: page 272 has '### ║5.11.3 Syntax Rules║', and page 271 has '### 5.10.4 General Rules'. It should be '### ║5.11.4 General Rules║'.

verdict.reasoning: The 300-dpi render of page 273 (VI-41) shows '5.11.4 General Rules' as the first line inside the boxed text, a subclause of 5.11 exactly like 5.11.1-5.11.3. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md, line 11543 is '## ║5.11 THE RENAMES CLAUSE║', lines 11545/11549/11559 are '### ║5.11.1 Function║', '### ║5.11.2 General Format║', '### ║5.11.3 Syntax Rules║', but line 11583 is '## ║5.11.4 General Rules║'. The heading text is present and correct; only its level is wrong (## instead of ###), which places 5.11.4 at the clause level in the outline. The rule text (GR1, GR2) is transcribed completely. A genuine structural defect, but the kind 'missing-heading' is inaccurate: nothing is missing.
verdict.corrected_description: Heading-level defect, not a missing heading: on page 273 the subclause heading '5.11.4 General Rules' is transcribed as '## ║5.11.4 General Rules║' (level 2, the level of '## ║5.11 THE RENAMES CLAUSE║') while its siblings 5.11.1-5.11.3 are level 3. It should be '### ║5.11.4 General Rules║'. Heading text and the general rules body are otherwise correct.
